item.title: GTA 6 Has Developers Praising Its Technical Ambition but Questioning Its Excesses
item.description:
GTA 6 has stunned veteran game developers with its technical wizardry and enormous scale, but some worry about its effect on industry expectations. Find out how several game industry veterans reacted to GTA 6.

Industry Veterans Compare GTA 6’s Technical Achievement to Magic


Developers Call GTA 6 Everything From Black Magic to Alien Intervention


Grand Theft Auto 6’s record-breaking launch made headlines, but some of its most nuanced praise has come from the people who understand how difficult it was to build. Game developers have marveled at Rockstar’s dynamic lighting, dense simulation, and interlocking systems, describing a technical achievement that appears almost impossible on current hardware. While the admiration is widespread throughout the games industry, some veterans worry about the excess and how it will raise expectations among players, publishers, and studio executives to levels most development teams cannot realistically meet.
Game industry veterans who have played GTA 6 have been stunned by its technical prowess, often describing Rockstar’s achievement in terms that make it sound closer to magic than conventional game development. Michael Barclay, a Naughty Dog veteran and World Design Director on Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, posted on X (Twitter) on November 20, saying "I’ve made video games for 19 years and GTA 6 appears to me as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child." In his post, he added that Rockstar’s environmental lighting is mostly dynamic yet looks as good as, if not better than, most baked lighting.
Naughty Dog game director, Mark Richard Davies, called GTA 6 the "Great Pyramids of Game Development" in a post on X on November 22. Davies joked that people will ask for centuries how it was made and that future generations will eventually conclude aliens made it. The former The Last of Us Part II designer was particularly impressed by "every NPC having voice lines and reactions," adding that the sheer size of the game’s script must be "mind-boggling."
Some developers have described Rockstar’s work as everything from "black magic" to "pure sorcery." Bethesda Game Studios design director Emil Pagliarulo, Odd Tales founder Tim Soret, and veteran character artist Del Walker were among those who described it as magic. Meanwhile, CD Projekt Red’s Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzyński, who called the game a "technological and creative miracle," and "probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history," joked that Cyberpunk 2 is now canceled because of his "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression."

Former Rockstar Lead Says GTA 6 Takes Eight Hours to Find Its "Magic"


Fans Are Divided Over the Game's Slower Pace


GTA 6’s most common criticism comes from the game’s slow start and push for realism, which draws more from Rockstar’s last title, Red Dead Redemption 2. Obbe Vermeij spent 14 years at Rockstar and served as technical director on GTA 3, Vice City, San Andreas, and GTA 4, classic titles that are receiving a wave of new players on PC. Although he did not work on GTA 6, Vermeij called the finished game "Very good," but argued that its first eight hours give players too little choice.
He said tutorials, cutscenes, mandatory missions, and basic objectives dominate Chapter 1, and agreed with complaints about "realism over gameplay" and an opening that "doesn’t feel like a sandbox" point to Rockstar’s early pacing rather than the entire campaign. Once Vermeij entered Chapter 2, he said that’s where the "GTA magic kicks in," since the game backs off, and that he’s been having loads of fun since then.
Our survey has echoed these similar sentiments and disappointments from players. When asked whether GTA 6’s 13-year wait has lived up to the hype, respondents ended in a tight 52.5% to 47.5% split, with players saying "Yes" coming out slightly ahead. The biggest criticisms of the game pointed toward the push toward realism and daily maintenance. Another survey expressed discontent with the lack of a true GTA sandbox, particularly pointing to reduced sexual content and freedom in the game.

Rockstar's Success Could Change What Developers Build Next


GTA 6 Is a $3.79 Billion Argument for Single-Player Games


GTA 6’s monumental success has led to concerns about how other developers and games will follow in its trail. Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier asked several game developers what GTA 6 could teach the wider industry in his November 25 video, "GTA VI Is Breaking Everyone’s Brains." Asher Einhorn, a veteran designer who worked at Naughty Dog and Archetype Entertainment, said that Rockstar has shown that developers can make "normal activities and interactions interesting." He believes that breakthrough could have a revolutionary effect on game design.
On the business end, Take-Two reported that GTA 6 generated an estimated $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales before its online component arrived, and Schreier said Einhorn and veteran artist Del Walker both saw single-player as the rare industry trend worth chasing. According to him, the number makes it increasingly difficult for executives or investors to maintain that "single-player games don’t make money," particularly after years of publishers chasing trends and pursuing live-service hits.
In a separate post on X, Larian Studios publishing director Michael Douse argued that "not every game needs to be GTA," adding that its rarity leaves space for other kinds of experiences. Schreier also reinforced the case for sustained investment in single-player-focused games, pointing to Elden Ring, Baldur’s Gate 3, and The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild as major successes created by veteran teams that were allowed to build on earlier work and refine their ideas across multiple releases.

Deus Ex Creator Questions Whether GTA 6’s Scale Is Worth Repeating


Image from Warren Spector's LinkedIn post
Deus Ex creator Warren Spector doesn’t believe that Rockstar’s production model should be celebrated without qualification. In his original LinkedIn post, he congratulated the team but questioned whether another studio should attempt a project with a reported billion-dollar development cost while thousands of developers remain unemployed. "Personally I’d rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is."
Spector argued that underfunding games or forcing them out before they are ready can guarantee failure, writing "no game that matters ships on time and/or on budget." Alan Wake 2 game director Kyle Rowley offered a pushback in his reply, calling Spector’s position "an awful message" for aspiring developers, while Remedy senior development manager Jani Pääjärvi said Control shipped on time and on budget and Control Resonant stayed within budget without a massive final crunch, detailing that the former’s budget was 30 million while the latter was 50 million.
Reactions from industry veterans suggest that GTA 6 is now a test of what the games industry chooses to learn from its success. Outside of taking inspiration from the game systems and secrets, can publishers and executives give more teams the time, stability, and creative freedom to develop ambitious games of their own? More importantly, will players keep supporting these experiences without expecting every studio to match Rockstar’s scale and near-unlimited budget?

item.title: FF7 Revelation Might Have Advent Children Content, Says Hamaguchi
item.description:
FF7 Revelation might have some Advent Children surprises in the form of costumes, but nothing’s confirmed, says director Naoki Hamaguchi.

FF7 Revelation Team Open To Adding Advent Children Content


Costumes, Characters, Maybe More


Final Fantasy 7 Revelation (FF7 Revelation) will have plenty of costumes for the characters and Advent Children costumes may just be part of them, director Naoki Hamaguchi said.
In an exclusive interview with GamerBraves, founder Sean Lim asked Hamaguchi if the team had ever considered bringing back the film in “a remake-style title or as part of Revelation content” in some form. Aside from the previously confirmed Sephiroth-themed and Vincent-themed DLC, he replied that nothing has been planned ahead of them just yet. However, the team is fully aware that fans want the chance to play as Advent Children characters or even have the option to wear the Advent Children costumes.
Hamaguchi didn’t deny or confirm the suggestion of Advent Children content, but entertained the thought by highlighting that Revelation’s new FITS and skin system will have “various costumes” for fans to enjoy.

No Plans For Ever Crisis Costumes


However, based on the interview, the Revelation team is only considering Advent Children costumes, as other spin-offs might be a bit harder to pull off. Outfits from the FF7 game spin-off Ever Crisis, which recently reached end of service in October this year, was also brought up.
It had many notable outfits that fans loved and would have wanted to see in a new form, but Hamaguchi quickly shut the idea down for now, saying that if they added one costume, then they’d have plenty of requests for the others: “So for now, we have no plans to bring costumes over from Ever Crisis.”
For now, fans will just have to wait patiently for more teasers to come as the FF7 trilogy finale’s launch draws near. Final Fantasy VII: Revelation will launch on Steam, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and Epic Games on April 8th, 2027.
Source:
EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: Naoki Hamaguchi on Final Fantasy VII Revelation, Advent Children & More

item.title: GTA 6 Shoe Ad Feels Like An FF7 Reference, and Fans Are Convinced
item.description:
GTA 6 players found a Final Fantasy 7 reference, according to fans who spotted a shoe ad in the game's social media content. Read on to learn what players noticed and other details here.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Shoe Ad Sparks Final Fantasy 7 Reference Theories


Hints Point to Cloud Strife, Aerith, and Zack


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) fans reported to have found a nod to Final Fantasy 7, and the clip of the reference is in a shoe ad. Said brand is called Eris, which seems to be a play on Nike’s brand.
In Greek mythology, Eris is the goddess of strife or discord, and another potential relation is found in the shoe model itself being named Strife, as it’s also the surname of Cloud, FF7’s main protagonist. Part of the theory also rests on the account name behind the ad, which fans read as a spelling of Aeris instead of @ERIS, the original English name of Aerith. The colorway in the add, black and red, also is visually similar to a Black Materia's.
Another thing that pushed many players toward the idea was a lone commenter on the post whose username is "Zackattack", which many believe it to be Zack. Zack Fair is a character from the Final Fantasy 7 series who is closely tied to both Cloud and Aerith, and fans joked that he would definitely pick that name for himself.
Others thought that the Greek goddess explanation could be enough on its own as a nod to mythology instead, but thanks to the account names, they felt it tip more toward Final Fantasy 7. Still, not everyone is convinced as some of the replies think that the ad could simply be a Greek mythology joke on the Nike name and that the rest is just pure coincidence.
Neither Rockstar Games nor Square Enix has commented on the ad at this time, so for now it remains fan speculation. With still much to discover, many players are combing Vice City for Easter Eggs, such as Red Dead Redemption 2’s Arthur Morgan’s cowboy hat. For more thoughts and insights on the game, check out our review below:

item.title: GTA 6 Keeps It Real With The Birds and Wildlife with Accurate Birding, Says Expert
item.description:
GTA 6 has a full bird-collection list among its heists and chases, and a birder tracked down all species and found that Rockstar's take is surprisingly faithful. Read on to see what the game has in store for its nature and the other details here.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Birds and Nature Praised for Realism


Birder Finds All 60 Species in About a Day


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has a quieter side that’s equally anchored in realism through its nature and wildlife. Nicholas Lund, a contributor to Audubon magazine, noted that he has birded extensively across Leonida, published a field guide on November 20 after completing it. He finds that Vice City's wildlife is built with care, even if it isn't 100% accurate.
The in-game menu lists 60 bird species. Lund notes that pre-release marketing mentioned 62, and that a few extra birds appear only on the hunting screen. He played for about two hours after midnight on release night and about six more on Thursday, reaching 50 species. A morning session covered a zoo and a farm, and his final bird was an American Barn Owl on a water tank in the northern part of the map. A Rockstar designer even replied to his post about finishing with a single word exclaiming: "History!"

What Rockstar Got Right and Wrong


The other main praise is for how the map handles habitat. Wading birds, shorebirds, and seabirds gather along the southern coast, while woodpeckers, Wood Storks, and American Robins appear farther north. Exotic birds that have settled in tropical South Florida, such as the Spot-breasted Oriole and Red Junglefowl, are also in the game.
Lund adds that the landscape itself is the most convincing part, from Keys mangrove beaches to marshes further north. Smaller touches, like roadside fruit stand lettering and roadkill along the highway, sell it too. He also notes that birdsong competes with car radios, horns, and heavy litter, which he jokes is a fair picture of birding in South Florida.
The game does bend some of the realistic factors for gameplay. However, Lund’s verdict is that GTA is meant to be fun, not science. Though as a birder, the game is decent at giving nature content, which isn’t the game’s main focus to begin with. Still, he points out the following:
  • Whooping Cranes and Red-cockaded Woodpeckers, both at-risk species in real life, show up commonly.
  • A Golden Eagle, very rare in Florida, circles the Mt. Kalaga area, where mountains don't exist in the real state either.
  • Some species have altered names, such as a Black-capped Chickadee instead of a Carolina and a "New World Oriole" instead of a Baltimore. He suspects this is because Carolina and Baltimore don't exist in the GTA universe.

Birds Aren't the Only Realism in GTA 6


The wildlife actually fits a wider pattern in the game. GTA 6 replaces the one-button car theft of older titles with a tiered vehicle security system, where older cars need a Slim Jim and a hotwiring mini-game, while newer ones need a digital key cloner and a disabled GPS tracker. Fuel management and heavier driving controls add to the effect, and texting behind the wheel is punished harshly.
Fans have split on whether this much detail helps or hurts the series' chaotic fun, but it shows Rockstar putting its detail into the world, apart from the missions. Others have also been comparing its extensiveness with Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption 2, with environmental details and interactions. For our own thoughts on the game, check out our review below.
Sources:
Audubon | I Tracked Down All 60 Birds in GTA 6: A Birder's Guide to Vice City's Wildlife
Alec McNamara | Response on X

item.title: Aether Gazer Global Content Updates End In December, But Servers Will Remain Active
item.description:
Aether Gazer's global version will stop receiving new content after Version 5.2, but the servers will stay online. The team has plans already lined up so read on to learn more about the content timeline.

Aether Gazer Global Ends Content Updates After Version 5.2


Servers Still Online, Top-Ups Disabled


Aether Gazer EN announced on X (Twitter) that content updates for the global version will officially end following the Version 5.2 update on December 1, 2026. The servers will remain online after updates end, so players can still log in as usual. Account registration and top-up services have been disabled on all platforms since November 24, 2026.
Additionally, an in-game refund page will be open from December 14 to January 14, 2027, letting players request refunds for all Shifting Flowers acquired since the open beta launch that remain unused. Refunds are based on each account's unused balance as recorded on December 8, 2026. The developers point players to a separate Refund Processing Plan Announcement for the specifics.
In the post, the developers acknowledged that the quality of much of the game's content fell short of player expectations and that the game struggled to reach the results they hoped for in the market. Despite this, they sincerely hope for the best and are grateful for the support.

Thank-You Gifts and the Choice Moment Event


After the Version 5.2 update, all players will receive a thank-you gift by in-game mail:
  • Precise Scan Voucher x90
  • Shinou-The Unawakened x1
  • Ring of Oath x1
  • Outfit Voucher x168

The update will also introduce a special event called Choice Moment, where players can claim one Modifier of their choice. The pool includes every Modifier, including those introduced in Version 5.2, but excludes collaboration limited-edition Modifiers.

By Your Side Update Moves Game to Long-Term Service


Following Version 5.2, the team plans to release a "By Your Side" update on December 29, 2026. It will adjust event gameplay, Scan rotations, and resource acquisition, and is meant to shift the game into a long-term service mode that keeps it running. As previously reported, global will receive all CN content first before transitioning to a companion server. Further details will come in future announcements. Listed below is the current schedule:
  • November 24, 2026: Account registration and top-up disabled on all platforms
  • December 1, 2026: Version 5.2 update and thank-you gifts
  • December 14, 2026 to January 14, 2027: Refund application page open
  • December 29, 2026: By Your Side update

The team closed by thanking players and saying they’ve taken both the criticisms and praise to heart as learning experiences. Reactions on X were mostly fond, with some players saying the game felt like it was just getting started, others saying they were sad to see it go, and a few wishing games like this had an offline version so the story could be preserved.
Source:
Aether Gazer EN on X | Aether Gazer Global Version: End of Content Updates Announcement

item.title: 100+ Things We Got as Gamers Before GTA 6
item.description:
GTA 6 took more than 13 years to arrive, during which the gaming industry has changed dramatically. Here are 100+ things we got in gaming before GTA 6 finally came out.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

A Lot Happened Between GTA 5 and GTA 6


13 Years Is a Long Time…


Grand Theft Auto V (GTA 5) launched on September 17, 2013. It took more than 13 years for Rockstar Games to release its sequel. During that time, the gaming industry went through two console generations, welcomed countless remakes and long-awaited sequels, and experienced big changes that reshaped how people play.
With GTA 6 finally here, let us look back at more than 100 notable things that happened in gaming during the wait.

Remakes, Remasters, and Rereleases


1.　The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time received a full remake on November 5, 2026, just 14 days before GTA 6 launched.
2.　Resident Evil 2, 3, and 4 were all remade in the span of four years (2019–2023), with Capcom releasing Resident Evil 2 in 2019, Resident Evil 3 in 2020, and Resident Evil 4 in 2023.
3.　Final Fantasy VII (FF7) became a multi-game remake project (2020–2024). Square Enix released FF7 Remake in 2020, followed by FF7 Rebirth in 2024. The third and final installment, FF7 Revelation, was announced with an April 8, 2027 release date in September 2026, before GTA 6 launched.
4.　The Legend of Zelda had several remakes and remasters: Wind Waker HD (2013), Majora's Mask 3D (2015), Twilight Princess HD (2016), and Link's Awakening (2019).
5.　Naughty Dog remade its 2013 adventure The Last of Us for PS5 as The Last of Us Part I, which launched on September 2, 2022.
6.　Crash Bandicoot's original trilogy returned in the N. Sane Trilogy in 2017. It was followed by Spyro's first three adventures in the Reignited Trilogy in 2018.
7.　Three horror games received modern remakes: Dead Space in 2023, followed by Silent Hill 2 and Until Dawn in 2024.
8.　Bluepoint Games remade Shadow of the Colossus (2005) and Demon's Souls (2009) for PlayStation. They were released in 2018 and 2020, respectively.
9.　Super Mario RPG and Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door were remade for Nintendo Switch in 2023 and 2024, respectively.
10.　Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire (2002) received full remakes for the Nintendo 3DS, titled Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, in 2014.
11.　Metal Gear Solid 3 received a full remake as Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater, which launched on August 28, 2025.
12.　Atlus released Persona 3 Reload in 2024, a full remake of the original 2006 PS2 RPG.
13.　BioWare brought the original Mass Effect trilogy together in Mass Effect Legendary Edition (2021).
14.　Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 (September 4, 2020) and Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 + 4 (July 11, 2025) brought back the first four entries in the classic skateboarding series as modern remastered collections.
15.　Nintendo remastered the original Metroid Prime for Nintendo Switch in 2023.
16.　Rockstar remastered GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas in Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy - The Definitive Edition (2021) to modern platforms.

Games and Franchises That Finally Got Developments


17.　Hollow Knight: Silksong was announced in 2019 before finally releasing in September 2025.
18.　Baldur's Gate 3 continued the mainline RPG series in 2023, 23 years after Baldur's Gate II originally launched in 2000.
19.　Kingdom Hearts 3 was released in January 2019, more than five years after Square Enix announced the game at E3 2013.
20.　Final Fantasy 15 underwent a big change. It was originally announced as Final Fantasy Versus XIII in 2006; the project was later reintroduced as Final Fantasy 15 in 2013 before launching on November 29, 2016.
21.　Final Fantasy XIV (FF14) received five expansions between GTA 5 and GTA 6: Heavensward (2015), Stormblood (2017), Shadowbringers (2019), Endwalker (2021), and Dawntrail (2024).
22.　Final Fantasy Brave Exvius eventually became the basis for Final Fantasy Resonance (2015–2026). Brave Exvius launched in Japan on October 22, 2015, and worldwide on June 30, 2016. Its global service ended on October 30, 2024, followed by the Japanese version on October 31, 2025. Square Enix then released an HD-2D remake of Final Fantasy Resonance on October 22, 2026.
23.　On October 26, 2018, Rockstar released Red Dead Redemption 2, a prequel to its 2010 Western adventure.
24.　Several long-awaited games finally made it out of development. Dead Island 2 was announced in 2014 and launched in 2023; Pikmin 4 was first mentioned in 2015 and arrived in July 2023; and Metroid Prime 4 was first revealed in 2017 and will release in 2025.
25.　Devil May Cry 5 continued the mainline series in March 2019, more than a decade after Devil May Cry 4 launched in 2008.
26.　Naughty Dog continued Joel and Ellie's story with The Last of Us Part II, which launched on June 19, 2020, seven years after the original game.
27.　Kratos left Greek mythology behind and entered Norse mythology in God of War (2018), followed by God of War Ragnarök in 2022.
28.　The Legend of Zelda reinvented its traditional formula with Breath of the Wild (2017), followed by Tears of the Kingdom (2023), which expanded Hyrule with multiple mechanics.
29.　Pokémon experimented with its traditional formula. Pokémon Legends: Arceus introduced a different catching system; Pokémon Scarlet and Violet brought the mainline series into a fully open-world format; Pokémon Legends: Z-A has real-time combat.
30.　Monster Hunter went from 4 Ultimate (2015) to World (2018) to Rise (2021) to Wilds (2025), with each major release expanding the long-running action series.
31.　Assassin's Creed became more of an open-world action RPG with Origins (2017), followed by Odyssey (2018) and Valhalla (2020), and Shadows (2025)
32.　Resident Evil moved into first-person horror with Resident Evil 7 (2017), followed by Resident Evil Village in 2021.
33.　id Software revived DOOM with a reboot in 2016, followed by DOOM Eternal in 2020 and DOOM: The Dark Ages in 2025.
34.　Yakuza changed its traditional combat system with Yakuza: Like a Dragon (2020). It became a turn-based RPG and introduced a new protagonist, Ichiban Kasuga. Its sequel, Infinite Wealth, was released in 2024.
35.　Supergiant Games released Hades in 2020 before launching Hades II in early access on May 6, 2024.
36.　Genshin Impact became a global gaming phenomenon after launching on September 28, 2020. It helped establish cross-platform gacha games as a major force in the gaming industry.
37.　No Man's Sky went from a controversial launch in 2016 to one of gaming's biggest comeback stories, with Hello Games continuing to release substantial free updates over the years.
38.　Cyberpunk 2077 went from a disastrous launch in 2020 to a major comeback with its 2.0 update and Phantom Liberty expansion in 2023.
39.　Blizzard replaced the original Overwatch with Overwatch 2 in October 2022. They transitioned the hero shooter into a free-to-play model.
40.　The Sims 4 became free-to-play on October 18, 2022, nearly eight years after its original release.
41.　Street Fighter 6 and Tekken 8 both arrived during the wait, with Capcom releasing Street Fighter 6 in 2023, seven years after Street Fighter V, and Bandai Namco releasing Tekken 8 in January 2024, nearly nine years after Tekken 7's arcade debut.
42.　Blizzard finally released Diablo IV in June 2023, 11 years after Diablo III originally launched in 2012.
43.　Metroid Dread is the first new 2D Metroid story in 19 years; it launched in 2021, following Metroid Fusion, which originally released in 2002. Nintendo announced Metroid Ravenous during the September 2026 Direct.
44.　Xenoblade Chronicles and Splatoon grew into major Nintendo franchises. Xenoblade Chronicles 2 and 3 launched in 2017 and 2022, followed by Xenoblade Chronicles X: Definitive Edition in 2025. Splatoon also received sequels in 2017 and 2022 after its original release in 2015.
45.　Super Smash Bros. Ultimate launched in December 2018 with every previously playable fighter in franchise history. It inspired Nintendo's famous Everyone is here! campaign.
46.　Mario Kart 8 Deluxe received 48 additional courses through the Booster Course Pass (2022–2023), which brought tracks from previous Mario Kart games to the Nintendo Switch across six waves.
47.　Several indie games became some of gaming’s biggest successes during the wait, including Undertale (2015), Stardew Valley (2016), Celeste (2018), and Balatro (2024).
48.　FromSoftware released Elden Ring in February 2022, one of the decade's biggest gaming hits.
49.　Half-Life returned with Half-Life: Alyx in March 2020, 13 years after Half-Life 2: Episode Two (2007). The VR-exclusive prequel was the first new full-length Half-Life game in years. Half-Life: Episode 3 has not been announced (yet).
50.　Microsoft released a new Microsoft Flight Simulator on August 18, 2020, 14 years after Flight Simulator X launched in 2006.
51.　Counter-Strike 2 replaced Counter-Strike: Global Offensive on September 27, 2023. Valve released it as a free upgrade to one of the world's most popular competitive shooters in the world.

Games That Were Rereleased on Other Platforms Years Later


52.　GTA 5 appeared on three console generations. It launched on PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2013, on PS4 and Xbox One in 2014, and eventually PS5 and Xbox Series X|S in 2022.
53.　Several major PC and console games arrived on Nintendo Switch, including Skyrim and DOOM in 2017, followed by Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus and Dark Souls Remastered in 2018.
54.　The Witcher 3, Cuphead, Ori and the Blind Forest, Alien: Isolation, and Divinity: Original Sin 2 all received Nintendo Switch ports in 2019.
55.　No Man's Sky, The Outer Worlds, and Apex Legends eventually came to Nintendo Switch in 2020 and 2021, followed by Persona 5 Royal and NieR: Automata in 2022.
56.　Several PlayStation exclusives eventually made their way to PC, including Horizon Zero Dawn (2020), Days Gone (2021), God of War (2022), Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered (2022), The Last of Us Part I (2023), and Ghost of Tsushima Director's Cut (2024).
57.　Microsoft began bringing several Xbox-published games to PlayStation, with Pentiment, Hi-Fi Rush, Grounded, and Sea of Thieves launching in 2024, followed by Forza Horizon 5 in 2025.
58.　Rockstar brought Red Dead Redemption to Nintendo Switch and PS4 in 2023, before releasing the original Western adventure on PC for the first time on October 29, 2024, 14 years after its original launch.
59.　FF14 expanded to another console platform when Square Enix brought its long-running MMORPG to Nintendo Switch 2 on August 4, 2026.
60.　Several Nintendo games received upgraded Switch 2 editions, including Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition in June 2026, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 in July, and Pikmin 4 on November 12, just seven days before GTA 6.
61.　Microsoft introduced backward compatibility for selected Xbox 360 games on Xbox One in November 2015, which allowed players to revisit older titles on its newer console.
62.　Sony began allowing PlayStation players to participate in cross-platform multiplayer with Xbox, Nintendo Switch, and PC players through Fortnite in 2018.
63.　Hotta Studio got tired of waiting for GTA 6 that they made a GTA-like mobile game in Neverness to Everness (NTE) on April 29, 2026.

New Consoles and Gaming Hardware


64.　The Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 were released in the gap between GTA 5 and GTA 6: the former in 2017, the latter in 2025.

69.　Sony and Microsoft introduced more powerful mid-generation consoles with the PlayStation 4 Pro (2016) and Xbox One X (2017).

Shakeups in the Gaming Industry


74.　Microsoft acquired Mojang and Minecraft for $2.5 billion in 2014, Bethesda's parent company ZeniMax Media in 2021, and Activision Blizzard in a $68.7-billion deal completed in October 2023.
75.　Sony expanded its first-party studios by acquiring Insomniac Games in 2019 and Destiny developer Bungie in 2022.

Gaming Trends and Cultural Moments

item.title: GTA 6 Is PlayStation’s Biggest Launch Ever, But CoD, Fortnite Lose Millions of Daily Players During Debut Weekend
item.description:
GTA 6 set a new record as PlayStation’s biggest launch ever. However, many live-service games saw declines in daily players during that same weekend. Find out which games saw the steepest drops and how Steam’s overall player activity compared.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Becomes PlayStation’s Biggest Launch in History


Sony Reports 39M PS5 Players in Four Days


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) has become the biggest game launch in PlayStation history; Sony Interactive Entertainment congratulated Rockstar Games after more than 39 million unique PS5 players played the highly anticipated sequel during its opening days.
According to Sony, players accumulated "683 million hours of gameplay" between November 19 and November 22, with "an average of 17.4 hours" per player. GTA 6 even surpassed previous PlayStation concurrent-player records "across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles" across five console generations.
The game’s launch also coincided with PlayStation’s largest single-day increase in newly connected PS5 consoles outside the year-end holiday period. Sony added that GTA 6 was the first game played on "70%" of those newly connected systems.
Independent figures from Circana further demonstrate the scale of GTA 6's debut. Mat Piscatella, Senior Director and video game industry advisor at Circana, reported that "61%" of active US PS5 players and 56% of active global Xbox players played GTA 6 on November 19. Those who played the game spent an average of "513 minutes" on PS5 and "494" minutes on Xbox, equivalent to more than eight hours on each platform.
Fortnite ranked second in engagement among active players across the two platforms; "10%" of players played Epic Games’ battle royale on the same day. Piscatella also identified Fortnite and Call of Duty among the five games most commonly played by people who experienced GTA 6 between November 6 and November 19. The other three are GTA 5 Remastered, Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

GTA 6 Launch Coincides With Player Declines Across Big Games


Call of Duty, Fortnite, Some Live-Service Games Suffer the DAU Drop


With such a historic launch, GTA 6’s release coincided with declines in the daily active player counts of several major live-service games, according to data from Alinea Analytics. In their November 23 report, analyst Rhys Elliott estimated that Call of Duty HQ, the centralized game hub for various Call of Duty titles, including Warzone, saw the steepest drop among the three major titles examined, followed by Fortnite and EA Sports FC 27.
Call of Duty HQ's estimated daily active users (DAU) fell by 42%, from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. The decline was even greater on PlayStation, where DAUs dropped by 44%. Four days after GTA 6’s release, Call of Duty remained 41% below its previous baseline. Alinea also reported that it recovered more slowly than the other games in its analysis.
Fortnite's estimated daily active users fell by 28%, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million. By the end of the launch weekend, its player count had recovered to within 19% of its usual baseline.
EA Sports FC 27 recorded a similar decline, with its estimated daily active users falling 27% from 5.9 million to 4.3 million. The game recovered to within 20% of its usual baseline by the end of Alinea's reporting period. Elliott also highlighted EA's efforts to retain players ahead of GTA 6’s release, including a 50% price reduction on the game and an early launch of its Thunderstruck promotion. The console discount began on November 13, with the Steam discount arriving on November 19. EA also introduced additional rewards and squad-building challenges as part of its promotional efforts.
Image taken from SteamDB
Separate Steam player-count comparisons revealed similar short-term declines among several PC games on November 19. A report from Ingenuity Fantasy Football found that Football Manager 27's daily peak concurrent-player count fell 14.6% from the previous day. Call of Duty recorded a 13.3% decline, followed by EA Sports FC 27 at 12.4% and Counter-Strike 2 at 9.2%.
SteamDB's longer-term chart also shows Call of Duty's Steam concurrent-player count falling from nearly 200,000 around November 7-8 to roughly 110,000 by November 17, before GTA 6's release.
Steam tracking research from Coilr provided further context, with Call of Duty recording approximately 27% fewer concurrent players than its historical baseline during GTA 6's launch week. However, Coilr found that Steam's top 100 games averaged just 1.9% fewer concurrent players than expected across the broader measurement period, a difference that remained within the range of normal weekly fluctuations.
Essentially, several major games saw noticeable drops in player activity around GTA 6’s launch, but Steam’s top 100 games as a whole remained close to their usual activity levels.
GTA 6's launch weekend drew attention to Rockstar's catalogue across generations. GTA 5, GTA 4, and San Andreas also broke player-count records during the same weekend. But for our take on GTA 6 itself, we've shared our thoughts in the review below.

item.title: GTA 6 Launch Weekend Sees GTA 5, GTA 4, San Andreas Player Counts Break Records
item.description:
GTA 6's console-only launch weekend caused GTA 5's player count to rise on PC, along with all-time highs from older titles like GTA 4, 3, Vice City, and San Andreas. Find out more details about the exact player counts below.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 5 Player Count Jumps on Steam During GTA 6 Launch Weekend


GTA 3, 4, San Andreas, and Vice City Achieve New Steam Peak


Grand Theft Auto 6 may currently be limited to consoles, but its early commercial success has sparked renewed interest in the series’ titles available on PC. According to SteamDB, GTA 5 Enhanced reached 137,993 concurrent players on Steam on November 22, its highest total since July’s Kortz Center Heist for GTA Online and one of its largest peaks since the upgraded PC version launched in March 2025.
Images taken from SteamDB
Meanwhile, GTA 5 Legacy has also seen a bump following GTA 6’s launch, recording a concurrent player peak of 101,616 on November 22. Beyond that, GTA 4: The Complete Edition set a new all-time concurrent player record, reaching 14,457 players on November 22. That day, the Definitive Editions of San Andreas, Vice City, and GTA 3 also hit their own all-time highs.
Rockstar’s previous game, Red Dead Redemption 2, has also received a new wave of active players on PC, reaching a concurrent peak of 69,766 players on November 22, its highest total for 2026. These figures cover only Steam, excluding anyone playing GTA on PC through the Rockstar Games Launcher or Epic Games Store.

When Is GTA 6 Coming to PC?


Rockstar's PC Release History Suggests 2027 or Early 2028


Rockstar has yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6, let alone provide an estimated release date. For reference, GTA 5 first released on consoles on September 17, 2013, with the PC version following 19 months later on April 14, 2015, while Red Dead Redemption 2 launched on consoles on October 26, 2018, and reached PC more than a year later on November 5, 2019.
Take-Two Interactive chairman and CEO Strauss Zelnick avoided providing further details during the company’s second-quarter earnings call on November 9, 2026. According to a transcript published by The Motley Fool on November 10, when asked whether rising console prices could accelerate GTA 6’s expansion to PC or streaming platforms, Zelnick replied that "any information about new SKUs (stock-keeping units) and the like will always come from our labels," leaving any future announcement to Rockstar Games and an even longer wait for PC players.
Speaking to Bloomberg in an interview published on May 4, 2026, Zelnick explained that Rockstar prioritizes consoles because it wants to serve what it considers the series’ core audience first. Zelnick also denied that a Sony marketing agreement was responsible for GTA 6’s console-first release, saying that Rockstar has historically launched its games on consoles before expanding to other platforms.
If GTA 6 follows a similar PC release schedule to Rockstar’s last two games, it may take more than a year before the game comes to PC. For now, fans are taking the time to experience the other games in Rockstar’s library while trying to avoid major spoilers, particularly since GTA 6 may have enough secrets and content to keep players exploring for years.

item.title: GTA 6 Has Enough Secrets and Content For “Years to Come,” Rockstar Says
item.description:
GTA 6 will have secrets, Easter Eggs, and hidden content that players will uncover for years, Rockstar says. Find out more details about how Rockstar continues their approach to letting players discover random encounters while exploring.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Will Have Secrets and Hidden Ambient Content For Years to Come


Secrets Require More Involvement from the Player


Rockstar hopes Grand Theft Auto 6 will keep players uncovering hidden content for years, with some of Leonida’s secrets only revealing themselves after repeat visits, at night, or through a series of encounters across the map. We asked Rockstar about this for our review, and Ghyan Koehne, Senior Design Director of Exploration & Ambient Content, explained that the studio built different layers of discovery into the world and that "players have new things to uncover for months and hopefully years to come."
According to Koehne, finding those secrets will sometimes involve more than reaching the right spot. He explained that "Some content exists at a single location, requiring only that the player find it and be observant, while some only appears on a repeat visit to an area, or at night."
Additionally, Koehne said some of this content involves interacting with unique NPCs, while other discoveries require the player to engage with the environment. "Some are single visit locations that tell a one-and-done story, some are a single location that evolves and tells a story over multiple visits spaced out over days, while other locations, once investigated, start the player on a journey across multiple locations and encounters."
The next segment contains spoilers for several references and surprises for random encounters, but nothing related to the story.

GTA 6 Easter Eggs and Secret Pays Homage to Florida


Rockstar Also Included References to Past Games


Since GTA 6 launched, players have already started sharing their discoveries and random open-world counters online. We’ve already spotted our share of easter eggs and secrets, especially local legends and other media set in Florida, like Dexter Morgan’s apartment, which references some of the Bay Harbor Butcher’s tools and locations. One longer Easter Egg starts after players spot Bigfoot roaming around Mariana County, which then unlocks a new contact that tasks the player with hunting the Skunk Ape cryptid.
Rockstar has also included references to their past games and shared universes, including several callbacks to Red Dead Redemption, like protagonist Arthur Morgan’s hat. The boat Michael De Santa stole in GTA 5 also appears in the game, and the GPS is still set to Los Santos, the setting of the previous installment.
Players can also find and scan four hidden posters scattered across the map, which unlocks a secret radio station hosted by Kodak Black. This unlockable Sniper of La Perle radio station primarily features Haitian sounds and rap, bringing the total count of GTA 6’s radio stations to 22.
The studio has a history of encouraging exploration with secrets, Easter Eggs, and hidden quests, while also spooking players with paranormal and eerie encounters. If GTA 6 follows or even exceeds the encounters from GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption, where the community is still discovering secrets until now, then it will truly be a long time before players have combed over everything there is to see and experience in Leonida.

item.title: Trickcal: Patima Global CBT Planned for Q2 2027, EPID Games Confirms
item.description:
Trickcal: Patima, EPID Games’ next project, had further details revealed, including plans for a global closed beta in 2027, and more details on the PC version of Trickcal: Chibi Go. Read on to learn more about developer’s highlights here.

Trickcal: Patima and Other News Detailed at G-STAR 2026


Trickcal: Patima’s global closed beta might just be around the corner. EPID Games' CEO Han Jong-hyun, Vice CEO Shim Jong-sun, and main PD Lee Hyun-seung revealed more details about Trickcal: Patima on November 20 during Korean gaming exhibition G-STAR 2026 with news that the game will go global and aims for a CBT in 2027.
In an interview with Japanese outlet 4Gamer, the game is dubbed a turn-based RPG, and the team cited Honkai: Star Rail as an inspiration and favorite of theirs. But instead of having just a battle-focused structure, the game also features relationship-building and lifestyle content.
Patima's alpha build video surprised the team with strong reactions in North and South America, as it became their most-watched video in North America. Chibi Go's earlier closed betas were Korea-only, but Patima will get a global CBT. Participant recruitment is planned for the first quarter of 2027, with the test itself in the second quarter, and at least two rounds. Han also said they'd like to exhibit at Anime Expo 2027 in the US if possible.
The alpha video also ended with the three leaders openly asking for publishers. They said they want to explore more options now that the company has grown, and that they haven't fallen out with Bilibili, Chibi Go's global and Japanese publisher, with whom they've also discussed these.

Turn-Based RPG About Running a Company


Story-wise, the protagonist is a senior employee at a company and, according to the team, the only human in the world. Players run the company from Patimachi, a hub aboard a ship. It includes a training academy, a production and cargo area, dormitories where you can cook, and a theater.
They added that Patima is meant to differ from Trickcal: Chibi Go, with sharper art lines and a target age of 15+ in Korea compared to 12+, though the team says it still has plenty of cute elements. The story connects to Chibi Go, but the developers have kept quiet about it as it contains plot spoilers. A prototype began in April 2025, and full development started this year, with about a third of the game complete already.

Chibi Go: PC Version and Story Updates


The Korean PC version of Trickcal: Chibi Go is planned for the end of November through Google Play Games, for stability and security reasons. The team also said an optimization specialist hired for the Korean version's third anniversary made loading about five times faster. The global PC version is still in preparation, with no date confirmed at this time.
On the other hand, the Japanese version is also moving forward. Han described its first year as an introduction to the world of Elias, and that the main story starts now. Then the global version will get additional stories and scenes. For the time being, though, Japan remains EPID's top priority market, and the team plans to go with a different approach for the Korea and Japan player base, respectively.

item.title: GTA 6 Features Weird Al and Janelle James on the Radio and Original Music From The Weeknd

GTA 6 has celebrity radio hosts and original music in Leonida, with credits to many artists, including Weird Al Yankovic and Lana Del Rey. Find out all the hosts and artists that players can hear while cruising through Vice City.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Features 22 Music Stations and Two Talk Stations


Star-Studded Radio Hosts Include Lana Del Rey, Bad Bunny, and Weird Al Yankovic


Pictured: Kodak Black at the Jack of Hearts strip club.
Grand Theft Auto 6's radio lineup brings together a star-studded cast of real-life musicians, actors, and comedians across 22 music stations and two talk stations, with several celebrities also helping write the material players hear. Rockstar’s official credits confirm the following music-station hosts, including presenters of shows within those stations, with some of them even posting on their socials about the extent of their involvement.
In Rockstar’s official credits, the studio's GTA TV & Radio section credits DJ Pooh and Joey Henson as the writing directors, alongside several senior and associate writers. The studio also credited a few of these hosts who helped with additional writing, namely Weird Al Yankovic, Doug Stanhope, Brian Posehn, Janelle James, and Stavros Halkias. In his Bluesky post, legendary parody artist Yankovic confirmed he helped write some of the in-game commercials and voices the Burger Shot ads, in addition to hosting Vice City FM.
  • AfroBank FM: Burna Boy as Burna and Jay Donaldson (Palms Trax) as Palmsy.
  • Back Country Radio: Morgan Wallen as MW, Lana Del Rey as Delta Dawne, and Jeremy Dufrene as roving reporter Mud Dog Mike.
  • CircoLoco Records Radio: Seth Troxler as DJ Seth and Antonio Carbonaro as DJ Antonio.
  • Cocoteo FM: Bad Bunny as El Martillo and RaiNao as La Gata.
  • Dirty South Classics: Trina and Trick Daddy as themselves, with Gucci Mane appearing as himself while hosting The Tap In.
  • Emotion 98.3: Doug Stanhope as Doug Van Dyke.
  • Flash FM: Robyn and Alex Consani as themselves.
  • Gloriana Blues Radio: Buddy Guy as DJ Buddy and Keith Richards as DJ Keith.
  • Honey FM: Chilli and T-Boz as themselves, with Craig Robinson as Liquid Wilson, hosting Liquid City.
  • Kaleidoscope FM: Jeremy Irons as DJ Dicky.
  • Leonida Jazz Radio: Randy Brecker as DJ Randy and Stanley Clarke as DJ Stanley, with Yussef Dayes appearing as himself while hosting The Nook.
  • Radio La Ola: Gloria Estefan as Gloria and Emilio Estefan as Emilio.
  • Radio On-U: Adrian Sherwood as himself.
  • Stockyard FM: The Dare as Harrison and PinkPantheress as Victoria.
  • Symphony FM: Yuja Wang as Yuja.
  • The Chamber 106.6: Kerry King as DJ Kerry, Tom Araya as DJ Tom, and Brian Posehn as Big Fan Brian.
  • The Sniper of La Perle: Kodak Black as Himself, presented by Michaël Brun
  • The Vault Radio: DJ Pretzel as himself.
  • Vice City FM: Weird Al Yankovic as DJ Al and Brigitte Nielsen as Madame Brigitte.
  • Vice City Rap Radio: JT as DJ JT and DJ Stevie J as DJ Stevie, with Charlamagne tha God as Charlamagne and Ivy Rivera as Ivy, hosting Early AF.
  • V-Rock: Lindsey Buckingham as The Buck and Michael McDonald as Skipper McD.
  • Worldwide FM: Gilles Peterson as himself.

GTA 6 also features two unlockable radio stations: The Sniper of La Perle and The Vault Radio. Hosted by Kodak Black and presented by Michaël Brun, the Sniper of La Perle features Haitian music and requires the player to scan four posters around the map. Meanwhile, DJ Pretzel hosts The Vault Radio that plays EDM, and players can unlock this by finding and scanning the associated poster inside The Vault nightclub.
Craig Robinson also helped create the music for Liquid City, the Honey FM show he hosts as Liquid Wilson. Rockstar’s credits list eight original songs for the show, with Robinson sharing songwriting credits on six of them.

Wipe and WKTT Provide Absurd Social Commentary


The Wipe and WKTT make up the game’s two talk-radio stations, following a more conversational style with GTA’s signature unhinged and satirical humor. Abbot Elementary star Janelle James voices Tish on She Got Assets for The Wipe, an opportunity she said she pursued with Rockstar. She also conceptualized, pitched, and scripted the show, adding that she’s been playing the game since Vice City.
  • The Wipe — Ask Dr. Nita: Anitta as Dr. Nita.
  • The Wipe — El Otro Lado: John Leguizamo as Enrique "El Enigma" Romero.
  • The Wipe — She Got Assets: Janelle James as Tish.
  • WKTT — The Richard Bastion Show: Jason Sudeikis as Richard Bastion.
  • WKTT — Hit the Bricks: Stavros Halkias as Dominic "The Brick" Brizzolato

GTA 6’s Original Score Brings Together Justice, The Weeknd, Djo and More


Rockstar Says Original Music Plays a Big Part for Jason and Lucia's Story


Rockstar partnered with Atlantic Records on Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a collection of 34 new recordings featuring artists including Lana Del Rey, Dua Lipa, Travis Scott, Cardi B, and JENNIE. Before launch, ten songs were released for streaming, but the whole album and even a separate vinyl release are available to purchase.
Alongside that album, French duo Justice composed GTA 6’s original score. Before launch, players could hear "Flower in a Hurricane," featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. At the time of writing, it has over 23 million views on YouTube, with the community hailing it as the game's theme song. Moreover, "Pusher," featuring Gesaffelstein, and "Starting From Zero," featuring Michael McDonald, also appear in the score and on the 34-track companion album.
Rockstar’s launch credits confirmed two further Justice collaborations with "My Only Vice," featuring The Weeknd, and "The Night’s Coming," featuring Djo. During a Q&A with Rockstar, we confirmed that it was an original track composed for the game. "Original music is a huge part of Grand Theft Auto’s identity, and it plays a big part throughout Jason and Lucia’s story," Rockstar said.
Music and radio have always been a huge part of GTA, giving each city its own sound and personality. Even as Rockstar rethinks familiar elements like sex workers and casual encounters, GTA 6’s celebrity radio hosts and original music keep that vibe going. item.title: NIKKE Gears Up for All-New Raid Rush, Winter Events, Upgrades, and Season 2 Plans

NIKKE releases their November Developer's Note and players can expect a year-end boss event, added upgrades, new events, and more. Read on to learn other details about the major highlights.

NIKKE Developer's Note Reveals Raid Rush, Season 2, Events, and New Features


Year-End Raid Festival and Union Ranking For the Major Update


NIKKE will be holding major events, added features, upgrades, and a Raid Rush, as announced in their November 2026 Developer's Note on X (Twitter). Director Hyungsuk Yoo opened the news by apologizing first for the PC launcher security issue, saying the team will keep taking follow-up measures even after compensating players with extra pulls. Raid Rush, which was first teased as the EX Raid, will be held once a year. Players can join through a login event, solo score-target challenges, or a Union Ranking competition.
The login event gives out gacha currency and growth materials without requiring boss fights. The solo challenges bring back all 12 bosses from this year's Solo Raids, and a player’s best score for each of the five Codes is added together to unlock additional rewards. In the Union Ranking, each Union picks one boss, and the combined scores of its top 15 members decide the standings. Rewards include a Raid Rush-exclusive Union Icon and Union Chips.

Birthday, Winter Event, and Season 2 Plans


On January 1, 2027, a birthday event starts in which the Counters Squad sends a short voiced story and an exclusive gift on a player’s registered birthday. Players can soon register their birthdays starting with the early December update, and the team plans to expand this type of content further.

item.title: GTA 6 Fans Reportedly Review Bombing Ocarina of Time and Soulcalibur on Metacritic
item.description:
GTA 6 fans are reportedly review-bombing classics such as Ocarina of Time, its remake, and even Soulcalibur on Metacritic after GTA 6's own user score sank. Read on to learn more about the scoring and other details here.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA Fans Are Review Bombing Zelda and Soulcalibur


Critic Tie Turns Into a User Score Feud


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) had a historic reception, but its fanbase is reported to have given mixed reviews and low ratings to other iconic titles such as Soulcalibur and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. GTA debuted with a 99 Metascore, matching the mark held since 1998 by Ocarina of Time, yet players have rated it around 5.5 to 5.6 out of 10 across more than 98,000 reviews.
Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake launched on November 5 and held a 9.6 user score from release. In the days that followed, that number started to fall over the weekend. It was then noted that the remake dropped to 8.4 with more than 45,000 user reviews, and the original N64 game had bumped down from 9.1 to 8.7 as well.
While unconfirmed, the feud reportedly began with a claim that it was the Zelda fans that first bombed GTA 6, though it's unclear where the trend actually started. On the other hand, much of GTA's feedback from players, along with other complaints, includes the game's 30 FPS cap, censorship in certain regions, objections to its female co-lead, and the way some mechanics feel tedious.
The bombing is seen to have spread beyond even Zelda, as some other reported GTA 6 supporters are posting negative reviews on Soulcalibur, the 1999 Dreamcast fighter title, due to Metacritic's ranking placing it third among the best games of all time. Posts summarized on X say its user score dropped to a mixed 7.4, with reviews stating pro-GTA chants or claiming other games are better. Others in the gaming community are currently pushing back, while asking for better moderation of user scores.

Other Fans Think Each Title Deserves Praise


Not everyone is taking sides, however. In a Reddit post, many debated that both games deserve celebration with the initial high scores, and multiple commenters agreed that fans can enjoy each game without taking frustrations out on other titles. But now, other fans across social media platforms are critical of the review bombing and wonder if user ratings should still be credible thanks to events like these. Others in the community were also questioning whether the critics' GTA 6 scores were even valid, with the users’ scores being much lower.
At this time of writing, no response from Metacritic has been released regarding the drop in ratings. Both GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time have been nominated for multiple awards this season. For our thoughts and insights on each game, check out our reviews below:

item.title: Devolver Digital Promised to Compete With GTA 6 and Actually Followed Through With Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed
item.description:
Devolver Digital keeps the pressure on Rockstar by releasing a remake of a beloved retro console action RPG the same day as GTA 6, as promised in 2025.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

Devolver Digital’s Marketing Stunts Keep The Gaming Community in High Spirits


Two GTA 6 delays ago, back in March 2025, when Take-Two was still standing firm on an autumn 2025 launch, Devolver Digital promised to release a game on the exact same date as GTA 6. However, GTA 6 was infamously pushed back to May 26, 2026, then to November 19, 2026, but the indie publisher stuck to its word with the release of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed.
Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed was released on November 19, 2026, and now joins The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake in the highly specific lineup of games created for retro platforms and rebuilt for modern systems, facing off against GTA 6.
Originally prototyped for the Game Boy Color—physical cartridge and all—developer Doinksoft and publisher Devolver Digital agreed that the game deserved a wider release. So they ported it to PC and created GTA 6-themed promo materials.
Devolver good-naturedly pokes fun at nostalgia-bait remakes and reboots with its newest title, whose Steam page reads: "Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is a spectacular remaster of the original remake of the unreleased action-platformer starring the most famous video game mascot of all time."
The cartoon platformer's pre-release trailer parodies Vice City's signature pink-and-blue hues and ultraviolence using Volvy and friends. Devolver even offered players a free copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed if they posted a video of themselves deleting their GTA 6 pre-load. Players responded in kind with videos of actual GTA 6 pre-load deletions tagged #MakeRoomForVolvy.
Following GTA 6's release and widespread player complaints about losing the option to hire prostitutes, Devolver playfully wrote: "We'll add prostitutes to Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed if that's what it takes to make a billion dollars a day."
GTA 6's release has been marked by intense anticipation and contentious launch choices, and now, the internet is rife with heated debates about cut features and thematic preferences. Amidst a watershed moment for the video game industry, Devolver Digital's playful marketing stunts for Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed provide much-needed levity; a reminder to everyone that gaming is about fun and community.

item.title: GTA 6 Cuts Sex Partners, Prostitutes, and Other Longtime Features, Rockstar Explains Why
item.description:
GTA 6 leaves out a classic open-world feature to solicit adult services, a feature dating back to GTA 3. Find out Rockstar's explanation for their choice and the initial fan reaction.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Leaves Some Longtime Series Traditions Behind


GTA 6 Drops the Ability to Solicit Adult Services


In Grand Theft Auto 6, players can no longer solicit prostitutes, ending a series tradition that’s been around since GTA 3. As fans and early reviews have documented, this feature isn’t in the launch version, and there’s currently no similar mechanic in the game.
In a Q&A with Rockstar, we asked if Jason and Lucia can have intimate relationships or sleep with others outside their partnership. Rockstar Vice President of Design Stephen Donkin didn’t give a direct answer. Instead, he talked about the overall design philosophy for GTA 6 and why some familiar features were left out.
"GTA 6 is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run," Donkin said. "While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in 6 has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon." He pointed out that Rockstar focused on improving the radio, wanted system, robberies, and car theft.
Donkin also said that "many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTA 6," since the studio focused on features that fit Jason and Lucia’s story. He didn’t list which features were removed, but in a separate interview with Kotaku, he confirmed that players can’t gamble at Leonida’s casinos, explaining that gambling didn’t fit the story and could upset the in-game economy.

Some GTA 6 Fans Want the Freedom to Make Jason Cheat on Lucia


Many longtime fans are unhappy with the change and have shared their frustrations on social media. Some question why Jason and Lucia’s relationship should limit these activities, since past GTA protagonists had more freedom to act outside the main story. In the previous title, players noted that GTA 5 let Michael solicit prostitutes even though he was married to Amanda.
Some fans have been more direct, saying they want the option to have Jason cheat on Lucia. Players have discussed whether infidelity could affect the couple’s relationship or change the story’s outcome. Others hoped the game would allow them to pursue other romantic interests like Mandy, a popular early-game side character who flirts with Jason and is suggested to be violent and possibly a serial killer.

Jason and Lucia’s Romance Is Supposed to Be Optional


Player Choice Only Goes So Far in GTA 6


Jason and Lucia will spend much of GTA 6 working together regardless of how close they become. In a September interview with Famitsu, Rockstar North Head of Development and Co-Studio Head Rob Nelson made clear that the romance itself is optional, saying, "whether they go through those situations together as a couple or simply as accomplices is up to the player."
The effort players put into the relationship affects what Jason and Lucia can do together, as Nelson told Famitsu that if players ignore the romance, they lose affectionate actions like holding hands and kissing, but investing in the relationship brings them back.
Players who aren’t interested in romance can still finish the story with Jason and Lucia as partners in crime. Still, fans have pointed out that these statements contrast with the removal of these nightlife activities, as it takes away one of the ways players could previously make choices outside a protagonist’s established relationship.
GTA 6 still offers players a lot of freedom, but Rockstar is setting clearer limits on the story. In keeping Jason and Lucia’s relationship the core of the story, the game had to sacrifice some of its older open-world freedoms that, historically, didn’t affect the main narrative. item.title: GTA 6 Launch Is Official Leave and Party Day For Several Studios, Brands and Even an Army Unit
item.description:
GTA 6 launched on November 19, and companies from Palworld’s Pocketpair to Logitech marked it with official leave, livestreams and office parties. Here is how the industry celebrated and what it shows about GTA’s pull today.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Launch Reshaped Work Schedules Worldwide


Launch Day Arrived With Cleared Calendars


When Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) went live at midnight on November 19, a wave of companies had already cleared their calendars for it. Some handed employees official leave to play, and others threw parties at the office. Many workers around the world simply requested the day off.
GTA 6 is the first numbered entry in Rockstar Games’ crime series in 13 years. Rockstar announced the November 19, 2026 date after an earlier delay from May. The game unlocked at midnight local time on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The rollout began at midnight in New Zealand and moved across time zones from Tokyo to Miami, which brought launch parties and some companies giving staff the day off.

Employers Saw the Absences Coming


The planning started well before launch week. Payroll processor Gusto reported that paid time off requests for launch day were up 9% compared with the two prior weeks. BambooHR data put requests for November 19 at 9% to 17% above a typical third Thursday in November, and a BambooHR spokesperson noted that a broader trend toward using paid time off more freely could also play a part. These figures cover requests, so they describe plans and leave actual attendance unmeasured.

Gaming Companies Granted Official Leave for the Launch


Pocketpair Gave Players on Staff Five Days Off


The most generous policy came from the developer of Palworld. Pocketpair announced on November 12 that it would grant staff special leave from November 19 through November 23, sharing an image of the internal notice on the official Palworld X account. The company framed the break as “an urgent five-day business trip in Vice City.” The notice added that “such a historic occasion deserves our full attention,” excused staff who planned to play from regular duties, and covered a weekend, so it used three leave days.
Leadership joined in. CEO Takuro Mizobe wrote that he would be “taking a break for a while to play GTA6 too.” Palworld and Craftopia updates were set to continue on schedule during the break.

Logitech Turned the Launch Into a Company-Wide Game Day


Logitech took a wider approach with “Logi Game Day.” Every employee, interns included, can take one day off to play a game of their choice, and the initiative is the first company-wide gaming day in Logitech’s history.
The company backed the policy with a stated rationale. CEO Hanneke Faber said, “It’s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time.” Chief people officer Elaine Laird added, “Play is not the opposite of work.” Logitech G general manager Robin Piispanen said Game Day “gives our team a shared purpose.”

Bulkhead and Other Businesses Scheduled Their Own Breaks


Bulkhead, the studio behind the tactical shooter Wardogs, set its break for the weeks right after launch. CEO Joe Brammer told Edge magazine the whole team would take December off following the game’s early access launch. The stated reason is rest after the early access launch and Season 2. Bulkhead pulled Season 3 content forward to November 12, a week before GTA 6 arrived.
Brammer’s advice to players covered the rest of the month: “Go play GTA 6, we need to detox.” The line shows how comfortable a studio can be with a release of this size sitting next to its own game.
Businesses outside gaming made similar moves. California-based Burger Motorsports suspended operations for the launch, citing employee scheduling conflicts, and planned to resume once staff had completed at least one mission. Fox29 reported that a US Army battalion at Fort Stewart offered a four-day pass to soldiers who reenlisted. In India, boAt offered an optional day off.

Launch Parties Marked the Release in Offices and Cities


Pocketpair, Logitech G and Fans Held Launch Events


Leave policies gave way to celebrations once the game went live. Reuters photographed Pocketpair employees playing GTA 6 at the company’s Tokyo office, and reported that the company threw a sushi party to celebrate the launch. The office party matched the tone of the original notice, which treated the release as a shared occasion for the whole team.
Logitech G scheduled a livestream from its San Jose headquarters on November 19, with general manager Robin Piispanen, a former competitive gamer, set to host.
Outside company walls, retail venues and gaming bars hosted their own events. A launch party at Grails Miami marked the midnight release on November 18, and players gathered at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on launch day. Together with the studio events, they showed that GTA 6 drew crowds in person as well as online.

GTA 6 Is the Most Influential Release in Gaming Right Now


Sales Estimates and Studio Reactions Show GTA 6’s Reach


The commercial picture is still forming. Sensor Tower estimated cumulative digital sales of $1.84 billion by release day, more than double the $800 million GTA V made in its first 24 hours. These are third-party estimates, and Take-Two has not shared pre-order data. Take-Two’s own numbers will be the ones to watch.
Take-Two’s leadership kept its focus on the present. During a TBPN interview on launch day, CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about a future Grand Theft Auto and replied that GTA 6 had only just gone live. The exchange shows how quickly attention moves to what comes next.
Reactions from rival studios point the same way. Pocketpair named the game in its leave notice, Bulkhead pointed its audience toward it, and Logitech tied its first Game Day to it. 80.lv also reported that other studios moved their own releases away from the launch window. The calendar now bends around a single date, and that is rare for any entertainment product.

Our Take: Official Leave Replaced the Sick Day


Our reading of the launch is that employers formalized what many workers were already planning. The companies above gave employees official time in advance, and Logitech’s release tied gaming to confidence and work performance. The practice also gives HR teams a template for the next release that moves millions of people at once.
GTA 6 now sets the schedule for work, for rival studios and for conversations about workplace culture. Whether the leave trend outlasts launch week is a question for the coming months.

item.title: GTA 6 Censored in Japan, Says No to Naked Jason and Tones Down Gore
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI features censored nudity and toned-down gore in its Japanese release compared to other regions. Read on to learn more about Jason showering in underwear, the blood and gore changes, and fan reactions.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Japan Release Alters Nudity and Tones Down Gore


Nudity Changes Leave Jason in Underwear During Shower Scenes


Grand Theft Auto VI has rolled out with noticeable regional edits in Japan, where players have found that nudity is covered up or altered compared to the international release. While players in other regions see full nudity in certain moments across the open world, the Japanese version keeps characters covered up even in private scenes.
The most talked-about detail among players is that Jason wears underwear rather than appearing nude during shower scenes, with similar clothing adjustments applied to other characters and NPCs. Some explicit scenes and beach or shower moments have either had extra clothing added or been cut back entirely, prompting disappointment from fans in Japan who noticed the difference right after launch.
Players also picked up on early hints before launch when store listings showed the Japanese download sitting roughly 1 GB smaller than the standard global build, coming in at around 208.73 GB on PS5 and 208.74 GB on Xbox Series X|S compared to roughly 209.91 GB and 209.86 GB elsewhere, alongside a CERO Z rating that lacked a sexual content icon. Many fans online pointed out how jarring it feels to have an adult rating while still seeing underwear during routine moments like taking a shower.

Blood, Gore, and Other Differences in the Japanese Version


Nudity is not the only area scaled back in Japan, as coverage from Japanese outlet Game Spark and player reports also highlighted differences in how blood and gore are handled visually. In the Japanese release, the option to adjust blood and gore intensity is missing, leaving less blood overall compared to versions in other regions.
Even with reduced blood effects and dismemberment adjustments, players noted an odd contrast where extreme violence like shooting someone's head off can still happen while nudity remains covered up. Meanwhile, other parts of the game such as strip clubs and drug use still appear in the world, showing how selective the regional adjustments are across Leonida.
For players looking to see everything from Grand Theft Auto 6 without regional cuts, the difference in Japan has become a major talking point right at launch.

GTA 6 Japan Fans Left Frustrated by Censorship


Clips and screenshots showing Jason taking a shower in black underwear quickly circulated online, sparking debate among players comparing the Japanese build with the uncensored release elsewhere. In other regions, Jason appears completely unclothed in the shower, making the added trunks stand out to fans paying close attention to regional differences.
Many players in Japan questioned why such strict edits were applied when public bathhouses and hot springs are a familiar part of their everyday culture, while others wondered why a game already carrying a strict 18+ age rating classification still needed nudity covered up. Across social media like Twitter/X, several commenters expressed frustration over feeling like they were getting a tamer version of a title that is already built around gritty adult themes.

item.title: GTA 6 Is Making It Really Hard to Actually Commit Grand Theft Auto
item.description:
GTA 6 has ditched the classic one-button carjacking system in favor of specialized tools, mini-games, and GPS trackers. Read to learn how players can steal parked cars in the game and what fans think about the new carjacking mechanics.
GTA 6 Walkthrough and Guides Wiki

GTA 6 Pushes For More Realism in Carjacking


Stealing Cars is Harder Than Ever Before


Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) makes stealing cars far more challenging than in previous titles, leaning into a more realistic criminal experience. For nearly three decades, the core loop of GTA has been dead simple: walk up to any vehicle on the street, tap a single button, and speed off. With the release of GTA 6, however, Rockstar Games has overhauled that signature formula, making the franchise’s namesake crime significantly harder to pull off.
As Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson explained in preview interviews ahead of launch, the studio wanted to move away from binary, one-button vehicle thefts. Instead, GTA 6 introduces a tiered vehicle security system where the difficulty of stealing a parked car depends entirely on its value and era.
Older models only require a Slim Jim and a hotwiring mini-game, while modern and luxury cars demand an unlockable digital key cloner. Even after boosting a high-end ride, players must disable its alarm and built-in GPS tracker to keep police from tracking their location. To know more about GTA 6’s new carjacking mechanics, check out our article on GTA 6 How to Steal Cars.
Of course, players can still bypass parked-car security by carjacking vehicles with drivers already behind the wheel, though doing so immediately draws witnesses and police attention in Vice City's denser, tighter streets. Combined with new fuel management mechanics and punishingly realistic driving controls—especially when trying to use your phone behind the wheel—GTA 6 turns what used to be an effortless reflex into a calculated risk.

Fans Divided on the New Car Stealing Mechanics


The new carjacking mechanics drew immediate online pushback, with players expressing concern that leaning too heavily into hyperrealism could detract from the chaotic, mindless fun GTA is known for. Fans across X (Twitter) and Reddit pointed out that stopping to complete tedious break-in mini-games on parked cars disrupts the momentum of intense shootouts and police escapes.
GTA 6 also blocks players from stealing cars near Jason and Lucia’s safehouses and specific story hubs, a restriction some fans feel undercuts the signature freedom of the franchise. However, others in the community defended the rule, arguing that boosting cars on your own turf is a terrible idea in real life anyway.
Regardless, GTA 6 continues to dominate the whole gaming community since it launched, sparking multiple discussions about the game leaving out sex partners, prostitutes, and other longtime features. To know more about our thoughts on Grand Theft Auto VI, check out our review below.
